[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Flight Punctuality",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "The probability that a regularly scheduled flight departs on time is P(D) = 0.83, arrives on time is P(A) = 0.82, and both departs and arrives on time is P(D ∩ A) = 0.78. Find the probability that a plane arrives on time given that it departed on time, and departed on time given that it has arrived on time."
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Loaded Die Square Outcome",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Consider the event B of obtaining a perfect square when rolling a die where even outcomes are twice as likely as odd outcomes. Given that the roll resulted in a number strictly greater than 3, determine the conditional probability of event B."
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Fair Die Independence",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Consider rolling a single fair six-sided die with event A defined as rolling an even number and event B defined as rolling a multiple of 3. Verify whether events A and B are independent by comparing P(A | B) with P(A)."
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Successive Defective Fuses",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A fuse box contains 20 fuses, of which 5 are defective. If 2 fuses are selected at random and removed in succession without replacement, find the probability that both fuses are defective."
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Two Urns Ball Transfer",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "One bag contains 4 white balls and 3 black balls, and a second bag contains 3 white balls and 5 black balls. One ball is drawn from the first bag and placed unseen into the second bag; find the probability that a ball drawn subsequently from the second bag is black."
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Emergency Vehicle Availability",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A town has one fire engine with availability probability 0.98 and one ambulance with availability probability 0.92 during an emergency. Assuming they operate independently, find the probability that both vehicles will be available when responding to an injury from a fire."
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Sequential Card Selection",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Three cards are drawn in succession without replacement from a standard 52-card deck. Find the probability that the first card is a red ace, the second card is a 10 or a jack, and the third card has a value strictly between 3 and 7."
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Urn Color Counts",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Two balls are drawn in succession without replacement from an urn containing 4 red balls and 3 black balls. Determine the sample space outcomes along with the corresponding values taken by the random variable Y denoting the total number of red balls drawn."
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Defective Item Indicator",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Components arriving from a production line are inspected and classified as either defective or nondefective. Define a binary indicator random variable X that takes the value 1 if a component is defective and 0 otherwise."
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Continuous Decay Waiting Time",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Consider measuring the exact time in seconds until a radioactive particle decays. Identify the continuous sample space corresponding to this measurement as a subset of the real numbers."
  },
  {
    "n": 11,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Defective Laptop Distribution",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A shipment of 20 laptop computers contains 3 defective units. If an institution purchases 2 of these computers at random without replacement, determine the probability distribution for the number of defective computers acquired."
  }
]
